label: sec:molecular-chains-rings-intro
html:
We assemble atoms into extended molecular structures. A molecular Hopf chain of length N composes N - 1 covalent bonds along a backbone, giving a tridiagonal linking matrix with free endpoint sites. To pass to closed rings, we replace the naïve picture — N pairwise Hopf links — with a single non-local invariant: the threading link T(2,N). Its braid word winds twice through every atom, and its Alexander polynomial records half the pairwise Alexander weight. A molecular Hopf ring binds atoms globally by the threading link rather than locally by Hopf links.

The remaining blocks read off the dynamical consequences. Open chains behave as topological springs. Ring closure is a topological phase transition. The transition state is the barrier where pairwise bonds dissolve before the threading link forms. The same mechanism explains ring super-stability.
